newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq shares continue slide amid tech concerns.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq shares continue slide amid tech concerns.

text.p: Nasdaq shares dropped further Wednesday amid continuing concerns that recent earnings warnings by key technology companies may signal a slowdown in the personal computer industry, traders said.
The Nasdaq composite index shed 5.24 points or 0.38 percent to 1379.67. The session was mixed with advancing issues outpacing losing issues at a ratio of 6 to 5 on total volume of 605 million shares.

"There's just a big storm cloud hanging over the techs. People are worried about earnings and until there's a clear signal that everything's going to be ok this quarter, it's tough to get buyers out there, even at lower prices," one trader said.

Rumors that Gateway 2000 Inc may warn of an earnings shortfall knocked other personal computer companies, traders said. Dell Computer Corp lost 3-3/8 to 104-3/4. Semiconductor giant Intel Corp shed 2-1/2 to 142-1/2. Microsoft Corp slipped 1-9/16 to 119-3/16.

Elsewhere, H.F. Ahmanson & Co abandoned its hostile bid to acquire Great Western Financial Corp, clearing the way for Great Western to merge with Washington Mutual Inc, which gained 1-1/16 to 54-13/16.
